texts.preamble: Gujarat Pulses Manufacturers' ... vs Union Of India on 22 May, 2020 Author: Bhargav D. Karia Bench: Bhargav D. Karia C/Sca/12488/2004 Cav Judgment
texts.facts: By this petition under Articles 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioners have prayed for the following reliefs : "(A) That this Honourable Court be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus and/or any other appropriate writ, order or direction, commanding the respondents to annul the impugned decision as reflected from the aforesaid communication of respondent no.3 at Exhibit "B" to the petition as well as from the communication of respondent no.1 at Exh."H" to the petition prohibiting the usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of Tuverdal in the State of Gujarat (B) That pending, admission, hearing and final disposal of the present petition, this Honourable Court be pleased to stay the implementation and operation of the impugned decision on the part of the respondents as reflected from the aforesaid communication of respondent no.3 at Exhibit'B" to the petition as well as from the aforesaid communication of respondent no.1 at Exhibit H to the petition and thereupon be pleased to permit the petitioners to continue to use castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of Tuverdal. (c) That this Honourable Court be pleased to award the costs of this petition to the petitioners herein And (d) That this Honourable Court be pleased to pass such other and further orders as the nature and circumstance of the case may demand." 2. Brief facts of the case are as under : 2.1) Petitioner no.1 is an Association of Persons and petitioners no. 2 to 16 are the members of petitioner no.1 Association dealing in the business of manufacturing and processing various kinds of pulses in the State of Gujarat. 2.2) Petitioner no.1 has been recognized by the State of Gujarat as an official forum for the purpose of entering into necessary dialogue on various issues pertaining to manufacturers of various pulses in the State of Gujarat. 2.3) It is the case of the petitioners that for the purpose of protecting pulses from insects since time immemorial in the State of Gujarat as well as in several other States of the country, castor oil is used as a medium of protection in the form of coating the pulses. According to the petitioners, after the seeds of Tuverdal are processed to bring into existence the final product called "Tuverdal" (also known as split pulses or Toordal or Arhardal or Pigeon Pea) a coating of castor oil is applied thereon which acts as a medium of protection and thereupon Tuverdal is saved from Gujarat Pulses Manufacturers' ... vs Union Of India on 22 May, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11934498/ 2 the attack of insects. According to the petitioners, castor oil is considered as the best available medium of protection in the form of coating of Tuverdal considering the climatic conditions prevalent in the State of Gujarat and habit of the people residing there. 2.4) In the year 1985, an objection was raised for and on behalf of respondent no.2 State of Gujarat and its concerned authorities with regard to the usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating for protecting Tuverdal on the ground that the same would have the effect of rendering Tuverdal as "adulterated food" within the meaning of the provisions embodied in the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short "Act 1954"). 2.5) The petitioners therefore, made representations before respondent no.2 and its authorities contending that castor oil is the best available medium of protection in the form of coating for the purpose of protecting Tuverdal from the attack of insects etc. It was further submitted that there is nothing in the Act1954, which can be said to be having the effect of classifying Tuverdal with usage of castor oil as an "adulterated food". 2.6) It is the case of the petitioners that considering the representations made by the petitioners, respondent no.2 State of Gujarat under the signatures of the Director of Food Health issued a communication stating that it has been decided as a matter of policy not to consider usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating for protecting Tuverdal as "adulterated food" within the meaning of Act1954. 2.7) It is the case of the petitioners that thereafter, respondent no.3 Commissioner, Food and Drug Control Department, State of Gujarat issued a communication dated 6th January, 2003 addressed to the petitioners and its members intimating that as per the instructions received by him, it has been decided to hold usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of Tuverdal and other items referred to therein as not permissible under the provisions of the Act 1954 and thereupon to treat Tuverdal subjected to such a coating of castor oil as "adulterated" within the meaning of the Act 1954. 2.8) The petitioners therefore, made representation dated 10th January, 2003, before the concerned Minister of State of Gujarat explaining as to how it would be irrational to prohibit usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating on the Tuverdal followed by the representation dated 15th March, 2003. The petitioners also sought an opinion of the Agriculture Science Centre of Gujarat Agricultural University in this regard. The petitioners received a communication dated 30th/31st July, 2003 signed by the Administrator (Training) of Agriculture Science Centre of Gujarat Agricultural University at Devgadhbaria, wherein it is specifically stated that usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of food grains and pulses protects the food grains and pulses from the attack of insects. Gujarat Pulses Manufacturers' ... vs Union Of India on 22 May, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11934498/ 3 2.9) The petitioners thereafter made representations from time to time before the respondents. It appears that thereafter a communication dated 11th/21st May, 2004 was received from the Joint Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, stating that it would not be possible to consider favourably the representation seeking continuance of usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of Tuverdal as a preservative as the National Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad has not favoured usage of castor oil considering its adverse effect on human health. 2.10) Thereafter it appears that the petitioners made various representations but the same were not found favourable and therefore, the petitioners have filed this petition with the aforesaid prayers. 3. This Court (Coram : Hon'ble Mr. Justice K.S. Jhaveri) passed the following order on 27th September, 2004 : "Mr. D. C. Dave learned advocate for the petitioners serves an advance copy of the petition to Ms. Nandini Joshi learned AGP for the respondents. Notice returnable on 12/10/2004. The matter be listed in the first board. In the meantime, no consequential action be taken, pursuant to the communications at Annexures `B' and `H' to the petition. Direct service is permitted." 4. Thereafter the matter was admitted by order dated 12th October, 2004 as under : "RULE. Ms. Joshi learned A.G.P. waives service of rule on behalf of the respondent nos. 2 & 3. Adinterim relief granted earlier to continue. Reply filed on behalf of respondent no. 3 is ordered to be taken on the record."
texts.arguments: It was submitted that as castor oil is thick and sticky in nature, insects find it difficult to move on the Tuverdal, which in turn prevents their growth at the place where Tuverdal is stored. 5.1) It was further submitted by Mr. Dave that castor oil contains ricinolic acid which is considered as effective in preventing growth of numerous species of bacteria, yeast and moths. It was contended that before Tuverdal is used for its ultimate consumption as food, the same is subjected to rinsing and as a result thereof, castor oil applied thereon as a medium of protection in the form of coating, gets dissolved in water and thereupon stands removed from Tuverdal. Gujarat Pulses Manufacturers' ... vs Union Of India on 22 May, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11934498/ 4 5.2) In such circumstances, it was submitted by Mr. Dave that communication dated 6th January, 2003 issued by respondent no.3 and further clarification issued by respondent no.1 by letter dated 11th/21st May, 2004 prohibiting the usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of Tuverdal and other pulses would not have the effect of rendering Tuverdal as "adulterated" within the meaning of the Act 1954. Reliance was placed on the definition of the term "Adulterated" as defined in clause (ia) of section 2 of the Act1954 which reads as under: "2. Definitions. In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires xxx xxx xxx [(ia) ] "adulterated"--an article of food shall be deemed to be adulterated-- (a) if the article sold by a vendor is not of the nature, substance or quality demanded by the purchaser and is to his prejudice, or is not of the nature, substance or quality which it purports or is represented to be; (b) if the article contains any other substance which affects, or if the article is so processed as to affect, injuriously the nature, substance or quality thereof; (c) if any inferior or cheaper substance has been substituted wholly or in part for the article so as to affect injuriously the nature, substance or quality thereof; (d) if any constituent of the article has been wholly or in part abstracted so as to affect injuriously the nature, substance or quality thereof; (e) if the article had been prepared, packed or kept under insanitary conditions whereby it has become contaminated or injurious to health; (f) if the article consists wholly or in part of any filthy, putrid, [***], rotten, decomposed or diseased animal or vegetable substance or is insectinfested or is otherwise unfit for human consumption; (g) if the article is obtained from a diseased animal; (h) if the article contains any poisonous or other ingredient which renders it injurious to health; (i) if the container of the article is composed, whether wholly or in part, of any poisonous or deleterious substance which renders its contents injurious to health; (j) if any colouring matter other than that prescribed in respect thereof is present in the article, or if the amounts of the prescribed colouring matter which is present in the article are not within the prescribed limits of variability; (k) if the article contains any prohibited preservative or permitted preservative in excess of the prescribed limits; Gujarat Pulses Manufacturers' ... vs Union Of India on 22 May, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11934498/ 5 (l) if the quality or purity of the article falls below the prescribed standard or its constituents are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability, but which renders it injurious to health; (m) if the quality or purity of the article falls below the prescribed standard or its constituents are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability but which does not render it injurious to health: Provided that, where the quality or purity of the article, being primary food, has fallen below the prescribed standards or its constituents are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability in either case, solely due to natural causes and beyond the control of human agency, then, such article shall not be deemed to be adulterated within the meaning of this subclause." 5.3) Referring to the aforesaid definition of the word "adulterated" it was submitted by Mr. Dave that clauses (a), (c) to (g), (i), (j), (l) and (m) are concerned, same would not have any application to the usage of castor oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of Tuverdal. It was therefore, pointed out that whether the remaining clauses (b), (h) and (k) would come into play so as to render Tuverdal on account of such usage of castor oil as "adulterated" within the meaning thereof or not is required to be seen. It was submitted that clause (b) provides that if the article contains any other substance which affects or if the article is so processed as to affect injuriously the nature substance or quality thereof, then only the same would be considered as "adulterated". It was therefore, submitted that castor oil does not affect the Tuverdal in any manner as it is only a medium of protection from the insects. Similarly clauses (h) and (k) provides that if the article contains any poisonous or other ingredients or contains any prohibited preservative or permitted preservative in excess of the prescribed limits, then only such product would be considered as "adulterated". It was therefore, submitted that the castor oil is neither poisonous nor injurious to health and as a matter of fact in Ayurveda, as it is a matter of common knowledge to all concerned, since time immemorial that castor oil is considered as having medicinal value for certain diseases and it is often recommended for oral consumption for solving stomach disorder. It was further submitted that castor oil is never used as a preservative upon Tuverdal and hence the question of invoking the application of the clause (k) would not arise. 5.4) It was submitted by Mr. Dave that there is a thick line of demarcation between something which is used in the form of protection and something which is used as a preservative. Learned Senior Advocate placed reliance upon the definition of term "Preservative" as per Rule 52 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short Rules1955) which reads as under : Gujarat Pulses Manufacturers' ... vs Union Of India on 22 May, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11934498/ 6 "Preservative means a substance which when added to food is capable of inhibiting, regarding or arresting the process of fermentation, acidification or other decomposition of food." 5.5) Referring to the aforesaid definition of term "preservative" it was submitted by Mr. Dave that in order to qualify a substance as a preservative within the meaning thereof, it should possess two fold things i.e. (i) such substance should have been added to food and (ii) such substance should be capable of preventing any substance from the process of either fermentation, acidification or decomposition of food. It was therefore, submitted that in facts of the case, castor oil is neither added in the food i.e. Tuverdal and it does not prevent in any manner Tuverdal from the process of decaying. It was submitted that the purpose of coating Tuverdal with castor oil is only to protect it from insects. 5.6) Learned Senior Advocate thereafter invited the attention of the Court to report of Gujarat Agricultural University dated 30th/31st July, 2003 to submit that by coating Tuverdal with castor oil, prevents insects to enter into Tuverdal. It was therefore, submitted that the impugned communications are required to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK] permitting the petitioners to apply castor oil as coating upon the Tuverdal so as to protect it from the insects. 6. On the other hand, learned advocate Ms. Krishna Rawal appearing for respondent no.1 Union of India relied upon the averments made in the affidavit in reply filed by Assistant Director of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to submit that the Central Government has enacted the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short "Act2006")to consolidate the laws relating to food and to establish the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India for laying down science based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption and for matters concerned therewith or incidental thereto. It was submitted that the Act2006 repeals all other food related enactments and orders including the Act1954. It was therefore submitted that petition has become infructuous in view of the fact that in exercise of powers conferred under section 92 of the Act2006 following regulations are framed : "6, In exercise of powers conferred under Section 92 of the Act, the Food Authority has made the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011; Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011; Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011; Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011; Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations, 2011 and Food Safety and Standards (Laboratory and Sample Analysis) Regulations, 2011 to carry out the provisions of the Act." 6.1) In view of the aforesaid Rules and various regulations, provisions of other food related orders listed in 2nd Schedule of the Act2006 have come into operation with effect from 5th August, 2011, and therefore, the petitioners are required to file a fresh petition, if any grievance survives. Learned advocate for respondent no.1 submitted on merits, as averred in the affidavit in reply : Gujarat Pulses Manufacturers' ... vs Union Of India on 22 May, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11934498/ 7 "5 I say and submit that the use of Castor Oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of pulses shall amount to addition of foreign matter. Castor oil is nonedible oil and harmful to human health and therefore its addition/coating to the pulses would render the pulses as "adulterated" within the meaning of the provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. b. I further say and submit that the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was an Act of the Parliament enacted in the fifty fourth year of the Republic of India to make provisions for prevention of adulteration of food. It is further submitted that the answering respondent had the mandate under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 to lay down provisions for the standards of food and the articles used in them to be in congruence with the health of an individual. It is submitted that the prime objective of the Act and the Rules was to eliminate the danger to human life form the sale of unwholesome articles of food or food that may be injurious to health, and to curb the widespread evil of food adulteration. It was intended to suppress the social and economical mischief, or any evil which attempts to poison, for monetary gains, the very sources of sustenance of life and the well being of the community. It is further submitted that under the Act and the Rule the answering respondent can prohibit the manufacture, sale etc. of articles of food which are injurious to health. It is submitted that the answering respondent has to perform its obligations as cast upon it by the constitution. The presence of castor oil in toor dal or in any other food is not permitted, hence presence of castor oil in toor dal shall to amount to being adulterated and enforcement agencies are entitled to prosecute the offenders who were selling toor dal with admixture of castor oil." 6.2) Referring to the aforesaid contentions, it was submitted by the learned advocate for the respondent no.1 that National Institute of Nutrition by letter dated February 27,2004 has given the following opinion with regard to permission to use castor oil on Tuverdal as a preservative which reads as under : "Please refer your No. P.15025/4/2004PH(Food) dated 4th Dec 04 regarding comments on the request of the President Gujarat Pulses Manufacturing Association, Anand to the Ministry of Health seeking permission to use Castor Oil on Toor Dal as a preservative. 7. Learned Assistant Government Pleader Ms. Shruti Pathak appearing for respondents no. 2 and 3 relied upon the averments made in the affidavit in reply on behalf of respondent no.3, wherein it is stated as under : "4. 7.1) Referring to the aforesaid averments, it was submitted by Ms. Pathak that castor oil is not a preservative and therefore, same cannot be used as preservative as recognized under the laws relating to Prevention of Food Adulteration. It was further submitted that any article which is not included in ClassII preservative is not permissible in law, to be used with any food item. I say and submit that the use of Castor Oil as a medium of protection in the form of coating in respect of pulses shall amount to addition of foreign matter.
